Company Overview

Docusign brings agreements to life. Over 1.5 million customers and more than a billion people in over 180 countries use Docusign solutions to accelerate the process of doing business and simplify people’s lives. With intelligent agreement management, Docusign unleashes business-critical data that is trapped inside of documents. Until now, these were disconnected from business systems of record, costing businesses time, money, and opportunity. Using Docusign’s Intelligent Agreement Management platform, companies can create, commit, and manage agreements with solutions created by the #1 company in e-signature and contract lifecycle management (CLM).

What you'll do

Docusign operates global, always-on services. To safeguard customer trust and empower our engineering teams, we are building the next generation of monitoring and troubleshooting capabilities.]

You will lead the engineering organization behind our AI-powered observability platform. Built to complement existing tools like Grafana, Prometheus, and Clickhouse/Azure Data Explorer , this platform addresses the challenges of information overload by making observability accessible to everyone. You will manage a multidisciplinary team of backend engineers, machine learning engineers, and data scientists to build predictive, automated insights while running a highly critical service with strict SLAs.

Manage high-throughput, real-time observability pipelines processing massive volumes of telemetry data across multi-region, multi-cloud environments

jobs.title: Director of Product Engineering
jobs.description:
Aduro is seeking an experienced Director of Product Engineering to lead and grow our product engineering team. This is a people-first leadership role for someone who thrives on building high-performing teams, championing strong engineering culture, and creating the conditions for talented developers — and the AI systems they now work alongside — to do their best work.

You will step into a team that is energized and taking real ownership. Our Lead Developers and the broader engineering team are actively contributing leadership and driving outcomes. Your job is to build on that momentum: strengthen the processes, structures, and practices that enable the team to excel, and serve as a strategic partner to leadership on architecture and technical direction — including how we govern and scale AI across the software delivery lifecycle.

This role reports directly to the CPTO. You will partner closely with our interim Head of Engineering through an active period of team development, and you will assume durable leadership of the product engineering team as that transition completes. We are looking for a steady, experienced hand who can carry a team through change with clarity and confidence.

Why Aduro?

We're not your typical fund administrators. We're modern, innovative, and backed by deep industry experience — allowing our venture and private equity clients to focus on investing while we handle the details. Engineering sits at the center of that promise: we are building an AI-forward platform for regulated fund-administration data, where auditability, correctness, and data stewardship are first-class concerns.

We thrive in a people-first culture where each team member can impact the success of the business. We invest heavily in training and development, provide ample opportunities for growth, and work hard to foster collaboration and community.

How We Use AI (and What We Expect)

We believe AI is a powerful accelerator for engineering — and we use it intentionally. We're looking for engineers and leaders who are problem-solvers first
: people who can frame the problem clearly, explore options, and use AI to move faster without compromising quality. The differentiating skill we hire for is not tool familiarity — most people can learn the tools — but the judgment to rigorously evaluate AI output and decide what to trust, what to discard, and what to escalate.

AI is not "extra credit" here. We expect leaders to operationalize AI
across the software delivery lifecycle so the team can continuously retool without sacrificing security, correctness, or maintainability.
Use AI to accelerate research, ideation, debugging, test generation, documentation, and refactoring.
Embed AI into the SDLC — PR workflows, test strategy, refactors and migrations, incident response, and runbooks — with clear, written standards for what "done" looks like.
Treat AI output as a draft. Human judgment and peer review are mandatory, and reviews must explicitly evaluate AI-assisted changes for correctness, security, and architectural fit.
Maintain quality guardrails as tools evolve: unit and integration tests, linting and static analysis, CI discipline, and lightweight evaluation and benchmarking where useful.
Follow responsible-AI practices: protect sensitive client and fund data, never paste secrets, and use only approved tools and workflows aligned with Aduro's internal AI usage guidelines.

Here Is The Type Of Work You Will Do

Team Leadership & Culture

Coach, mentor, and develop engineers at all levels, with particular focus on empowering Lead Developers and reinforcing a culture of ownership and accountability.
Foster an inclusive, high-trust environment where engineers feel supported, challenged, and invested in the team's success.
Keep the team aligned, motivated, and focused through periods of growth and change.

Engineering Process & Execution

Evaluate, refine, and build on the processes and structures currently being established with the team.
Drive continuous improvement in how the team plans, ships, and iterates — championing best practices in Agile/Scrum, code review, documentation, and delivery.
Ensure the team has the right tools, workflows, and operational support to work efficiently and sustainably.

Architecture & Technical Direction

Set and maintain architectural direction in partnership with engineers and leadership — engaging substantively in technical trade-offs and validating AI-assisted design decisions, without needing to be a hands-on developer.
Own the governance model for agentic systems — agent scope and escalation paths, what data agents may access, how errors propagate, and the guardrails for security, reliability, testability, and cost — in partnership with the CPTO and security/data governance. This is a responsibility you'll hold directly.
Establish standards for evaluating AI-assisted and AI-driven work: output validation, lightweight eval/benchmarking, and cost considered at the architecture level rather than as an afterthought.
Ensure technical debt is tracked, prioritized, and addressed in a structured way, and help the team make sound build / buy / integrate decisions.

Cross-Functional Partnership

Work closely with Product, Design, Data Engineering, and other stakeholders to align engineering capacity and priorities with business goals.
Translate business requirements into clear engineering objectives; help the team navigate competing priorities with clarity and confidence.
Represent engineering in leadership and planning conversations, advocating for the team's needs and capabilities.

Hiring & Team Development

Partner with Talent Acquisition and leadership to grow the team thoughtfully — defining roles, conducting interviews, and onboarding new engineers effectively.
Develop a deliberate team-composition strategy for the AI era that balances senior leverage with a sustainable pipeline of growing engineers — avoiding an inverted, "senior-only" structure that erodes future capacity.
Develop career paths and growth frameworks that reward ownership, sound judgment, and technical excellence.

What Success Looks Like In Year One

The team's momentum has been sustained through the leadership transition, with Lead Developers operating with expanded ownership and clear growth paths.
AI is operationalized across the software delivery lifecycle, with written standards for review, quality, and what "done" means for AI-assisted work.
Platform capabilities that enable AI-powered workflows — such as agentic document ingestion, agent scaffolding, and the integration of AI components with our core deterministic systems of record — are moving forward with clear direction, set in partnership with the CPTO and Product.
A governance model for agentic systems is defined and operating, with guardrails the team understands and follows.
A deliberate team-composition and hiring strategy is in place and actively shaping how the team grows.

The salary range for the Director of Product Engineering position is $175,000 - $225,000. Salary is determined based on current market data and candidate experience level. This role is eligible to participate in the Aduro Bonus Program.

You May Be Successful In This Role If

10+ years in software engineering, with 6+ years in engineering leadership (Engineering Manager, Senior Engineering Manager, Director, or equivalent).
Demonstrated experience leading through other leaders (Engineering Managers, Lead Developers, Staff+ engineers) and scaling delivery across multiple workstreams.
A strong track record running the full people-leadership cycle: hiring, onboarding, performance management, coaching, and career development and leveling.
Experience building and operating durable engineering processes: planning and estimation, sprint or iteration rituals, prioritization, incident management, and continuous improvement.
Demonstrated experience operationalizing AI across an SDLC at team or organizational scale — not just personal tool use — with defined standards for quality and review.
Judgment for output validation and AI-system governance: reviewing AI-assisted code and architecture for correctness, security, and fit; and defining agent scope, guardrails, and escalation paths.
The ability to engage meaningfully in architectural discussions and technical trade-offs without needing to be a hands-on developer.
Experience guiding teams through transitions — organizational, technical, or cultural — with a calm, structured approach.

Nice to Have

Experience at a growth-stage or mid-size technology company.
Background in fund administration, fintech, or another regulated / data-sensitive domain.
Familiarity with agentic architectures, eval/benchmarking practices, or AI cost optimization at the system level.

Lead Time for Changes: under 24 hours for services
Change Failure Rate: under 10% trending down

Quality gates block merges: coverage thresholds, mutation score, static analysis, SAST, dependency and license scanning, SBOM generation
Contract testing (consumer-driven) between every service boundary; OpenAPI and AsyncAPI versioned and governed
Chaos engineering in staging, quarterly game days, production-like load testing ahead of peak retail events
Shift-right validation: synthetic monitoring, canary analysis, error budget enforcement
Own metrics: defect leakage, change failure rate, cycle time, escape rate, production incident rate

AI-assisted engineering: requirement decomposition, design-to-code, test generation, refactoring at scale, PR review
Agent-driven workflows: defect triage and clustering, root cause analysis from telemetry, release readiness scoring, customer-reported incident classification

SLOs and error budgets defined for every customer-facing service; error budget exhaustion blocks feature work
Observability-as-code: OpenTelemetry instrumentation is required before merge; service.version tagged; traces, metrics, and logs correlated by default
Performance engineering: load, stress, endurance, and soak testing sized for peak retail events (Black Friday, holiday, payroll cycles)
Edge resilience: stores survive network partitions; offline transaction handling; store-and-forward retry with exponential backoff and jitter; blue/green at the edge
Horizontal scale to tens of thousands of lanes across multi-tenant, multi-region deployments
Capacity planning tied to FinOps: cost per transaction tracked and optimized, not assumed

Platform Engineering & Developer Experience

Treat the engineering org as the customer of an internal developer platform (AI Dev Portal as the front door)
Golden paths: paved roads for new services, standard observability, standard security posture, standard CI/CD
Self-service environments: CloudOps Sandbox, on-demand synthetic test data, ephemeral preview environments per PR
Developer productivity instrumented: DORA plus SPACE metrics; time-to-first-commit for new hires; PR review latency; local build time

Professional Services Engineering Model

Customer-specific extensions delivered without fragmenting the platform
Config-driven first, code-driven by exception. Every bespoke extension has a sunset plan or a promotion path to core.
Reusable solution accelerators for common retail integrations (payments, peripherals, back office, tax, loyalty, CRM)
Integration contracts versioned and governed; breaking changes require deprecation windows and migration tooling
Clear engineering handoff to customer operations and support, with runbooks, dashboards, and on-call rotations live at go-live

Release Governance and Operational Readiness

Engineering-driven Release Gates, Not Process Theater

Functional completeness, validated by automated acceptance
Performance validation against published SLOs
Integration stability, with contract tests green
Observability live (dashboards, alerts, runbooks) before traffic

Rollback tested, not assumed

Security and Compliance Engineering

Software supply chain: SBOM generation, signed artifacts, SLSA build-level targets

Own outcomes, not tasks
Think in systems and data, not features
Hold the room at the customer executive table

We are an advanced robotics company developing intelligent humanoid robots designed to operate safely and effectively in real-world environments.
The company is building a full-stack robotics platform combining AI, robotics software, hardware and human-centred design to develop capable robots for a broad range of applications.
Backed by a major technology organisation, the business has the resources to pursue ambitious long-term robotics development while maintaining the pace and flexibility of a high-growth technology company.
The long-term ambition is to make advanced humanoid robotics practical, reliable and commercially viable at scale.

About the Role

We are looking for a Chief Technology Officer
to own the company's overall technology strategy and technical direction.

This is a company-wide leadership position spanning long-term technology strategy, product and R&D direction, robotics architecture and the development of the engineering organisation.
You will work closely with the CEO and senior leadership team to determine where the company should focus its technical investment, how the robotics platform should evolve and what capabilities need to be built to move from advanced R&D into reliable commercial products.
You will ultimately be responsible for bringing together the full robotics stack, from actuators, electronics and embedded systems through controls, planning, perception, AI and data infrastructure.

This is not a purely strategic CTO position. You will be expected to maintain strong technical depth, challenge engineering decisions, set architectural direction and get involved in the hardest technical problems when required.

Own and define the company's long-term technology strategy and technical vision
Translate the company's commercial and product ambitions into a clear technology and R&D roadmap
Work alongside the CEO and senior leadership team to determine technical priorities, investment areas and build-versus-buy decisions
Own the technical architecture and evolution of the humanoid robotics platform
Define and execute the long-term R&D roadmap across hardware, software, AI and robotics
Lead and develop the entire technical organisation across hardware, mechatronics, electrical engineering, embedded systems, controls, software, AI/ML and robotics

Set technical standards, architecture principles, engineering processes and development practices across the organisation
Drive innovation across manipulation, loco-manipulation, autonomy, perception and humanoid robot hardware
Oversee development of the full control stack, including state estimation, whole-body control, MPC and learning-based policies
Ensure hardware, firmware, controls, software and AI teams are working from a coherent system architecture
Establish the technical approach for taking advanced robotics research through development, validation and into reliable real-world deployment
Ensure the technology roadmap balances technical ambition with product requirements, development speed, cost and commercial priorities
Make final technical decisions on major architecture and platform-level questions
Develop a culture of high technical standards, ownership, experimentation and execution
Represent the company's technology vision externally with customers, strategic partners, investors and the wider robotics community
Protect and develop the company's core technical differentiation and intellectual property
Maintain sufficient technical depth to engage directly with the most challenging engineering and research problems

Qualifications

Master's or PhD in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering or a related technical discipline
10+ years of experience across advanced robotics, AI/ML or a closely related technical field
Significant experience working with humanoid, legged or highly complex robotic systems
Proven experience leading large, multidisciplinary engineering or R&D organisations
Track record of taking advanced robotics technology from research through development and into working physical systems
Experience operating at senior executive or technical leadership level, with responsibility for setting technology strategy rather than simply delivering against an existing roadmap
Demonstrated ability to recruit, develop and retain high-performing technical teams

Technical Requirements

Deep technical expertise in robotics software architecture and AI systems for humanoid or legged robots
Advanced experience with learning-based approaches including reinforcement learning, imitation learning, behavioural models and vision-language-action systems
Strong understanding of applying learning methods to robotic locomotion and manipulation
Hands-on experience with real-time robotics systems and ROS/ROS2 or comparable robotics middleware
Strong understanding of the full humanoid robotics stack, including actuators, sensors, electronics, embedded systems, controls, planning, AI and data infrastructure
Experience integrating hardware and software across complex robotic systems
Strong understanding of robot controls, planning and state estimation
Experience with production or field deployment of sophisticated robotic systems
Knowledge of model-based approaches including MPC, optimal control and LQR
Strong understanding of simulation, data generation, training infrastructure and the systems required to develop learning-based robotics at scale

Leadership Profile

The successful candidate will be a technically credible leader who can move comfortably between company strategy, engineering organisation design and detailed technical discussions.

They will be expected to:
Set a clear technical direction and bring the organisation with them
Make difficult technical decisions and take responsibility for the outcome
Know when to stay at the strategic level and when to get into the technical detail
Challenge assumptions and raise the technical bar across the organisation
Build strong relationships across engineering, product and commercial teams
Communicate complex technical ideas clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders
Balance long-term R&D ambition with the realities of building a commercial robotics company
Operate with high ownership, urgency and accountability
Build an engineering culture where people are expected to solve difficult problems rather than work around them
Be comfortable operating in an environment where the technology is still evolving and many of the problems do not have established answers

What Success Looks Like

In the first few years, the CTO will establish the technical foundation for the company's next stage of growth.

Success will mean:

A clear and credible technology strategy aligned with the company's commercial ambitions
A world-class technical leadership team and engineering organisation
A coherent architecture across the full robotics stack
Faster progression from research concepts to working robotic systems
Significant advances in locomotion, manipulation and autonomous behaviour
A repeatable process for developing, validating and deploying increasingly capable humanoid robots
A technology platform that can support the company's transition from advanced R&D into scalable commercial deployment
Clear technical differentiation that creates a lasting advantage in the humanoid robotics market

This is a people-first leadership role for someone who thrives on building high-performing teams, championing strong engineering culture, and creating the conditions for talented developers — and the AI systems they now work alongside — to do their best work.

We are looking for a steady, experienced hand who can carry a team through change with clarity and confidence.

Why Aduro?

We're not your typical fund administrators. We're modern, innovative, and backed by deep industry experience — allowing our venture and private equity clients to focus on investing while we handle the details. Engineering sits at the center of that promise: we are building an AI-forward platform for regulated fund-administration data, where auditability, correctness, and data stewardship are first-class concerns.

We thrive in a people-first culture where each team member can impact the success of the business. We invest heavily in training and development, provide ample opportunities for growth, and work hard to foster collaboration and community.

How We Use AI (and What We Expect)

We believe AI is a powerful accelerator for engineering — and we use it intentionally. We're looking for engineers and leaders who are problem-solvers first
: people who can frame the problem clearly, explore options, and use AI to move faster without compromising quality. The differentiating skill we hire for is not tool familiarity — most people can learn the tools — but the judgment to rigorously evaluate AI output and decide what to trust, what to discard, and what to escalate.

AI is not "extra credit" here. We expect leaders to operationalize AI
across the software delivery lifecycle so the team can continuously retool without sacrificing security, correctness, or maintainability.
Use AI to accelerate research, ideation, debugging, test generation, documentation, and refactoring.
Embed AI into the SDLC — PR workflows, test strategy, refactors and migrations, incident response, and runbooks — with clear, written standards for what "done" looks like.
Treat AI output as a draft. Human judgment and peer review are mandatory, and reviews must explicitly evaluate AI-assisted changes for correctness, security, and architectural fit.
Maintain quality guardrails as tools evolve: unit and integration tests, linting and static analysis, CI discipline, and lightweight evaluation and benchmarking where useful.
Follow responsible-AI practices: protect sensitive client and fund data, never paste secrets, and use only approved tools and workflows aligned with Aduro's internal AI usage guidelines.

Here Is The Type Of Work You Will Do

Team Leadership & Culture

Coach, mentor, and develop engineers at all levels, with particular focus on empowering Lead Developers and reinforcing a culture of ownership and accountability.
Foster an inclusive, high-trust environment where engineers feel supported, challenged, and invested in the team's success.
Keep the team aligned, motivated, and focused through periods of growth and change.

Engineering Process & Execution

Evaluate, refine, and build on the processes and structures currently being established with the team.
Drive continuous improvement in how the team plans, ships, and iterates — championing best practices in Agile/Scrum, code review, documentation, and delivery.
